messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: p99 streaming latency 15.2s (SLO breach) for dedicated-pool-east-1. Queue depth rising, streaming stalls reported. Paging oncall and eng-sre. See dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/streams?panel=dedicated-pool-east-1

alice (oncall): on it. grabbing p95/p99 panels and logs now. which customers are impacted?

ben (eng-sre): I see a big jump in queue depth at 15:02 UTC. p95 ~1.1s but p99 ~15s, tail is dominated by streaming stalls/kv-warmup. autoscaler hasn't added nodes in last 8m.

carmen (serving-runtime): looking at runtime logs — several workers failing warmup handshake with model shards: "warmup_timeout: kv-cache-init exceeded 30s". streaming sessions stuck waiting on KV restore.

alice (oncall): copy. runbooks: try manual scale + reroute / fallback model. ben, erin can you check autoscaler logs and node provisioning?

erin (infra): autoscaler shows pending scale up, but cloud API returned rate-limit 429 twice. provisioning queued. I'll retry manual request and bump priority.

ben (eng-sre): running quick checks, queue snapshot:
```
# queue snapshot (dedicated-pool-east-1)
pending_requests: 842
inflight_streams: 128
avg_latency_p95: 1.12s
avg_latency_p99: 15.2s
workers_ready: 18/22
```
Looks like workers are coming up but not finishing warmup. warmup concurrency seems to be the bottleneck.

carmen (serving-runtime): warmup logs excerpt:
```
2026-03-14T15:05:21Z worker-19 warmup INFO kv_cache restore start
2026-03-14T15:05:53Z worker-19 warmup ERROR warmup_timeout: kv-cache-init exceeded 30s
2026-03-14T15:06:04Z worker-19 runtime WARN streaming stall waiting for kv
```
So new workers are timing out on KV restore under the burst.

dave (support): we have 12 tenants with increased latency, 3 on higher-tier Dedicated contracts. Customer-ops ticket created INC-7892, pushing status.

alice (oncall): mitigation plan (short):
1) manual scale +4 replicas (infra)
2) route traffic for high-volume customers to fallback model variant (smaller quantized) to relieve warmup demand (runtime)
3) temporarily reduce per-worker warmup concurrency to avoid overloaded remote storage (runtime)
4) notify customers and provide ETA (support)
I'll lead coordination, assigning owners below.

erin (infra): executing manual scale now:
```
infractl pools scale --name=dedicated-pool-east-1 --delta=4 --priority=urgent
```
Requested 4 more nodes, cloud accepted, provisioning started. ETA ~90s.

ben (eng-sre): while infra scales, Carmen can you flip routing? small change in routing rules to send heavy tenants to fallback-model-v1-quant. Command to runtime: `route set --pool dedicated-pool-east-1 --from=prod-model-v2 --to=fallback-model-v1-quant --filter=tenant in (A,B,C)`

carmen (serving-runtime): applying routing patch now. patch applied, rollout 10%. increasing as we confirm. Also lowering warmup concurrency from 6 -> 2 on new workers to reduce parallel KV pulls.

incident-bot: AUTO: manual scale completed (4 nodes added) at 15:07:23 UTC. New workers registered but warmup still in progress.

ben (eng-sre): after routing and scale we see queue depth falling:
```
pending_requests: 220
inflight_streams: 54
p99: 2.1s
```
p99 dropped from 15.2s -> 2.1s in ~3m after mitigation. Still monitoring for streaming stalls.

alice (oncall): progress update to customers: "We're seeing decreased tail latency after manual scaling and routing changes; investigating root cause of warmup/kv restore timeouts. Next update in 20m." dave, please send to impacted list now.

dave (support): message posted to INC-7892 + emailed impacted customers (list attached). No major SLA hits yet but on watch.

frank (pm): which upstream change could cause sudden kv warmup pressure? did any config roll out recently?

carmen (serving-runtime): checking config history — no recent model or runtime config rollouts in last 24h. However, we ingested a hot prefix cache flush from a large tenant ~14:58 UTC that triggered many cold KV restores simultaneously. That aligns with burst start.

ben (eng-sre): that sounds like a thundering-warmup problem: single event (cache flush) caused massive concurrent restores. Need short-term throttles and longer-term protections (backoff, staggered warmup).

alice (oncall): immediate post-mitigation actions:
- ben/erin verify autoscaler rate-limit retry/backoff and add guard for faster manual override (ben)
- carmen implement staggered warmup and a capped concurrency per-tenant (carmen)
- dave finalize customer comms and log who saw errors (dave)
- frank own postmortem and timeline for mitigations (frank)
Set owners and times.

ben (eng-sre): created ticket INFRA-4123 to add autoscaler rate-limit handling and manual-priority flag. assigning to erin.

erin (infra): will add retry jitter + backoff to provisioning and a prioritized fast-path for oncall manual overrides. ETA EOD.

carmen (serving-runtime): opening RUNTIME-2510 to add staggered warmup, per-tenant warmup caps, and a routing fallback when KV restore queue > 1000. ETA next sprint for full fix, but I can ship a limiter hotfix within 48h.

alice (oncall): good. final status: p99 steady ~1.9s for 5m, queue normalized. marking incident as mitigated. leaving open for postmortem and customer followups. If anything regresses ping this thread.

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED at 15:13:18 UTC — p99 back within SLO. Incident doc: https://incidents.internal/2143654321 (assigned to frank for postmortem).

frank (pm): I'll own the postmortem. please drop logs, timelines, and comms into the incident doc. aim to have draft within 48h.

alice (oncall): handing off to owners: ben (infra followups), carmen (runtime fix), dave (customer comms), frank (postmortem). Closing oncall handoff now. :white_check_mark:
